paragraphs: R’ Yose son of Bun [ברי׳ בון] (II).

Hyman describes him as R’ Mana’s student: in Sheviit, chapter 6, halakhah 2, he heard from R’ Mana. In Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 11:2 [1:2 in the supplied Hebrew], R’ Mana’s students would say to her, “Show what is in your hand.” R’ Yose son of R’ Bun said to them: “Since she is to swear at the end, even about what is in your hand they say to her: tehi [תהי].”

He disputes R’ Mana’s words in Sheviit, chapter 6, halakhah 7; at the end of Ketubot, chapter 1, halakhah 5; and in Eruvin, chapter 5, halakhah 7. Hyman notes several other occurrences of R’ Yose son of Bun in the Jerusalem Talmud and calls him the later one. Hyman says this R’ Yose son of Bun had a son named R’ Shmuel; there is also a mention in the Jerusalem Talmud, Demai, chapter 4, at the end of halakhah 1. In his days, Hyman says, ALL the academies of the Land of Israel had already been destroyed.

notes.text: The “show what you hold … tehi” wording remains difficult and is not turned into an invented ruling. Hyman’s son Shmuel statement, later-Yose identification and claim about the academies are preserved as his assertions.

No new primary scalar was returned. The earlier bounded Venice Ketubot 1:2 nonmatch is inherited; no whole fresh Ketubot/PeneiMoshe text or missing legal ruling is claimed. שמע is heard from, not a separately established study event. The heading’s compressed ברי׳ בון is retained literally beside the provisional son-of rendering. Whether this compressed form includes an abbreviated father-title is not settled here; no full Rabbi title is established there. The later בי ר׳ בון separately supplies an abbreviated father-title. All personal ר׳ and compressed titles remain R-prime, including Mana, Yose and Shmuel; no full Rabbi title was obtained. אמר להו says he said to THEM, restored independently of the students saying to HER. The unresolved תהי phrase is retained without a reconstructed ruling. סוף markers סה״ה/סה״א give ends of halakhot 5/1; not sub-halakhot. Hyman’s later-Yose identification, son Shmuel and destruction of ALL academies remain his historical claims. After the son-Shmuel clause, the implicit subject of is also mentioned is not expressly restated; no new genealogical identity is admitted.

Hyman’s print cites Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 11:2 (פ״יא ה״ב), where the consulted witness has the discussion of a widow who has taken funds for her maintenance. Mana’s students say to her “show what is in your hand,” with הוי in the consulted Guggenheimer Hebrew and חוי for the students in the other consulted text. Yose answers the students, and his reply ends with the formula “they say to her: tehi.” Penei Moshe explains that she is to keep what is in her possession, since she must swear when she collects her ketubah. Korban HaEdah gives an alternate wording that expressly says they do not ask her to show it. Hyman’s printed heading has בר׳ בון, beside the supplied ברי׳ בון. The consulted Sheviit 6:2 has Yose asking Mana a question, Ketubot 1:5 and Eruvin 5:7 give separate disagreements, and Demai 4:1 names Shmuel son of Yose bei Rabbi Bun. The exact reported Sheviit 6:7 numbering remains unverified.
